rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary condition from < to <= causing thread 8 to read uninitialized shared memory shared[8] instead of using the neutral element 1.0. Since only 8 warps exist (256 threads / 32), only shared[0..7] are populated with valid warp products. The garbage value in shared[8] is multiplied into the final reduction result, corrupting the output.
rounds.kill_strategy: Use a tensor of all 1.0s so the expected product is exactly 1.0. The mutant will multiply in garbage from shared[8], producing a result that differs significantly from 1.0.
rounds.recommendations: When computing number of warps for shared memory reads, ensure the boundary condition exactly matches the number of warps that wrote data. Use '<' not '<=' when the count equals the valid index range size. Consider zero-initializing shared memory to make such bugs deterministic.
